_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform, distinct from the shared ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🔣️oracle.json manifest: that file registers `lopdf` under the `pdf-edit`/`pdf-parse` capabilities its own cases exercise; this file registers the SAME package under a distinct id and the `pdf-1-7-mutate` capability this subset's exhaustive mutation case (`mutate-pdf-1-7`) actually tags, per the wave 7 fleet brief's oracle-registration gotcha (reusing the shared entry fails the contract with `oracle-capability-mismatch`). 🧾️ The manifest declares all sixty kinds production dispatch offers. The sixteen page and COS-graph kinds are claimed by the thesis differential case `mutate-pdf-1-7` through the `pdf-1-7-base` catalog; the forty-four resource, catalog, page and identity kinds that ticket 26/09/18/PDF-ARTIFACT-SPEC-COMPLETE added are evidenced by lopdf-generated before/after pairs (🏭️generator/🔁️codec, registered below) and held to them by `🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🧪️tests/⚖️lopdf-vectors`, which applies each kind, writes the result with this subset's writer, reads it back and requires lopdf's after-document — then requires the inverse to write back to the before-document.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED by the `reimplementation-registered-as-third-party` gate. The crate named here does real work — it parses and writes this format — but what a MUTATION SHOULD PRODUCE is computed by this owner's own `🔮️oracles/🦀️.rs`. Both halves of the comparison then descend from ONE reading of the specification, so a misreading of it yields two agreeing wrong answers: the single failure a differential test exists to prevent.

The honest split is that the crate discharges "the result is a well-formed file of this format" and NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for, so this is a `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute, and a qualifying third-party reference is still owed.

Any fixtures registered alongside are untouched and remain valuable: real bytes of the real format, byte-reproducible, and exactly what a qualifying reader gets pointed at the day one is registered.

📖️ A READER, over a corpus that had to be REBUILT before one could mean anything.

The previous generator imported `oracle_apply_mutation` and `project_conformance` from `semio-s-plugin-stdio-test-oracle`, this repository's own crate, so the mutated bytes AND the expected projection of them were both ours and `lopdf` was a codec for our own answer. Registering a reader beside that corpus would have changed the label and nothing else.

`⚖️lopdf-engine` depends on `lopdf` and nothing else: it lays out the seed, performs each mutation through lopdf's own public COS API, and reads the conformance axes back through it. It refuses to write a pair whose projection does not move, so a no-op cannot be committed as a fixture that would pass forever.

The two encryption kinds are `-uncarried`, not routed around: lopdf 0.44's writer takes its encryption path whenever the trailer carries `/Encrypt` and then needs the encryption state a genuine decryption would have recorded, so a synthetic encryption dictionary can be neither written nor read back. A writer-side limit, not a reader gap.

comparisonProfiles.description: The generic pdf@1.7/base structural axes: the page list IN ORDER (so move-page is observable), each page's MediaBox/CropBox/Rotate and content bytes, the /Info entries, the catalog and trailer marker entries, and an object inventory by /Type — the axis a page-level projection alone would miss for insert-object and remove-object.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways for all 60 committed mutation pairs, per fixture, with the reader built from 🏭️generator/🔁️codec: (before,before) -> equal:true for 60/60; (before,after) -> equal:false for 60/60 — 120/120 directions correct. The projection now also renders every page dictionary, the catalog (minus its page tree), the trailer /ID and whether the file was encrypted, which is what makes the 44 resource, catalog, page and identity kinds observable. Observability is also enforced at GENERATION time: the engine refuses to write a pair whose projection does not move. The encryption pair reads back through lopdf's own empty-user-password decryption; the 16 arbitrary /U padding bytes lopdf draws at random are zeroed through the COS API, so it regenerates byte-identically.

60/60 kinds: the kind's own (before,after) compares equal:false
The reader projects and compares; it neither applies a mutation nor computes an expected state
The corpus regenerates byte-identically (two consecutive runs diffed equal); no wall-clock, no randomness in the seed, and the one random field lopdf's encryption writes is settled
lopdf 0.44.0 is vendored in the cargo registry cache; builds and runs with --offline
